unkind: Slamming the door in her friend's face was very unkind.
Saying thank you to the dinner lady is kind, not unkind.
A gentle person would never be unkind to a tiny kitten.
unfair: The game was unfair because one team had more players.
My sister got a bigger slice of cake, and that is unfair!
Is it unfair that I must go to bed before my brother?
untidy: Please put your shoes away, because the hall looks untidy.
His handwriting was so untidy that nobody could read it.
The garden looked untidy with long grass and fallen leaves everywhere!
unlock: Which key will unlock the little box on the shelf?
She turned the small silver key to unlock her bike.
Mum took out her keys to unlock the car.
dislike: I dislike wet socks, so I wear boots when it rains.
Do you dislike loud noises like the vacuum cleaner?
I really dislike getting up early on cold winter mornings!
disagree: Some people say tea is nicer, but I disagree!
My friends disagree, so we will take a vote.
Do you disagree with me about the best ice cream flavour?
misspell: I often misspell words that have double letters in them.
Did you misspell a word when you wrote the card?
Writing too fast can make me misspell easy words.
mislead: A picture on the box can mislead you about what is inside.
Do not mislead the visitors by telling them the wrong way.
Did the broken clock mislead us into thinking we were late?
dishonest: Did you tell the truth, or were you dishonest?
Saying the dog ate your homework when it did not is dishonest.
A dishonest fox in my story tells lies to get the cheese.
misbehave: Our class will lose playtime if we misbehave in assembly.
Please do not misbehave in the library, where everyone is reading.
Mum asked us not to misbehave on the long bus journey.

rejected.s: Is it unkind to ignore someone who wants to play with you?
rejected.reason: checker: 'Is it unfair to ignore someone' also makes sense, so the gap has two answers. (also fits: unfair)

rejected.s: It is unfair when one child gets three turns and you get none.
The race felt unfair because I started further back than everyone.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Than everyone' is unnatural (it should be 'everyone else'), and the shape copies the game sentence.

rejected.s: I need the key to unlock the front door.
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: shares a run of 4 words with the example

rejected.s: My cat will dislike the rain and stay inside.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Will dislike' is unnatural English for a habit.

rejected.s: She will dislike the smell of onions, so we left them out.
rejected.reason: checker: 'Will dislike' with 'left' mixes tenses in a way that sounds wrong.

rejected.s: Will the spell checker tell me if I misspell a word?
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: word overlap with the meaning is 50%

rejected.s: Oops, I will misspell my own name if I rush!
rejected.reason: checker: 'Will misspell' is unnatural here ('might' would be normal).

rejected.s: It is dishonest to say you finished your homework when you did not.
A dishonest child told Mum the dog had eaten the biscuits.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: capital word not allowed: Mum

rejected.s: Is it dishonest to keep a toy you found in the park?
rejected.reason: checker: 'Unfair' or 'unkind' could also fit, so the gap has more than one answer. (also fits: unfair, unkind)

rejected.s: Copying a friend's answers and saying they are yours is dishonest!
rejected.reason: checker: Cheating is also unfair, so a child could put unfair in the gap. (also fits: unfair)

rejected.s: Will the twins misbehave if we stay up late at the party?
rejected.reason: checker: The switch from 'the twins' to 'we' is confusing, and the link to staying up late is unclear.

rejected.s: The dishonest shopkeeper said the old apples were fresh.
rejected.reason: checker: A child could reasonably put unfair here, because selling old apples as fresh feels unfair. (also fits: unfair)

rejected.s: I felt dishonest when I told a lie about my drawing!
rejected.reason: checker: Saying you felt dishonest is awkward English, and the exclamation mark does not suit the sentence.
